title: Replenishing dispensers and consumables without contaminating new stock
audience: Cleaning staff who service washrooms and sanitary areas in healthcare facilities
learningOutcomes: Replenish soap, towel and tissue dispensers in the right sequence
Avoid contaminating new stock during refilling
Check dispensers for faults and report them

instruction.heading: Replenishing is part of the washroom clean
instruction.body: Replenishing is not a separate chore that can be done in any order. Check whether the dispenser needs refilling, then open it as the maker directs, damp-dust its outside, the nozzle or pump and its bracket, and discard the cloth under local policy. Refill or replace the contents without overfilling, close the dispenser, and then check that the kit is clean and back in its place.

instruction.heading: Handling stock
instruction.body: Open new packs only when they are needed for refilling. Do not leave stock on the ground or on a ledge where dirt can settle on it. Overfilling a dispenser can stop product coming out correctly, which wastes stock. Look for foreign material inside the unit before refilling.

instruction.heading: Refill or replace, and faults
instruction.body: Where a dispenser takes a refill pack or cartridge, replace it rather than topping up an old container. The SA standard does not accept topping up of liquid soap and disinfectant containers, and it expects those containers to be disposable. Report cracked, broken or faulty dispensers, and any scale deposits, to the supervisor. Do not clean dispensers with hand hygiene products; use the washroom cleaning product approved for the area.

procedure: Check whether the dispenser needs refilling.
Open the dispenser as the maker directs.
Damp-dust the outside, the nozzle or pump, and the bracket.
Discard the cloth under local policy.
Refill or replace the contents without overfilling, close the dispenser again and test that it works.

workedExamples.situation: A washroom paper towel dispenser is jammed, and a torn pack is found inside it.
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not force the mechanism or leave stock on the floor. Remove the foreign material carefully, check the mechanism, refill with a new pack that is opened only when refilling happens, and report the unit if it is faulty.

commonErrors.error: Overfilling so that product does not dispense
commonErrors.prevention: Fill to the level the maker sets.

commonErrors.error: Opening stock early and leaving it on a shelf
commonErrors.prevention: Open new packs only when refilling.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Use the maker's instructions to open each dispenser. Do not force locks or mechanisms.
The Irish method statements for dispensers are not Australian requirements. The SA standard governs for toilets and washrooms, and it does not accept topping up of liquid containers.

qualityStandard: The learner replenishes a dispenser in the stated order
The learner states why new stock is not opened early
documentationEvidence: Washroom clean checklist with dispensers replenished
Fault report for any dispenser that cannot be fixed on site
summary: Replenishing is part of the washroom clean and follows an order
Open new stock only when it is needed
Replace refill packs rather than topping up old liquid containers

knowledgeChecks.question: When should new stock be opened?
options: As soon as it is delivered
Only when it is needed for refilling
On a fixed weekly day for all dispensers

knowledgeChecks.question: Why avoid overfilling a dispenser?
options: It looks untidy, and visitors may think the store is poorly kept
Product may not dispense correctly, and stock is wasted
It makes the washroom too warm

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the SA standard's position on topping up liquid soap or disinfectant containers?
options: It is recommended for small sites that use little product
Topping up is not acceptable; containers are meant to be single-use
It is required at the end of each shift for every container in the store
